Simulation
Collisions — Momentum & Energy (guided inquiry)
Concept
Momentum Σmv is conserved in EVERY collision; kinetic energy is conserved only in elastic ones — the lost KE becomes heat and deformation.
Serves
Apply momentum conservation; distinguish elastic from inelastic; read ΔKE = −½μ(1−e²)u²rel; check Galilean frame invariance of ΔKE.
Inquiry
Equal masses, +2/−2 m/s, they stick. Do they stop because momentum was destroyed with the lost KE — or was momentum zero all along?
Misconception
If kinetic energy disappears when objects stick, momentum must disappear too.

Welcome toCollisions

Two carts meet on a frictionless track. You set the masses, the speeds and how bouncy the impact is.

How would you like to begin?

Listen to the intro

Guided Inquiry

1 · Two carts on a track

Here’s our setup: two carts slide on a frictionless track and meet head-on. Each one carries momentum p = mv and kinetic energy KE = ½mv² — we’ll keep an eye on both through every crash.

The restitution e sets how bouncy the impact is: at e = 0 the carts stick together, and at e = 1 the impact is perfectly elastic. Let’s see what each of those does.

2 · Striking a cart at rest

Let’s start simple. A cart strikes an identical cart at rest, and the two stick together. What do you think — what fraction of the original kinetic energy does the pair carry afterwards?

3 · Head-on and equal

Now let’s make it symmetric. Two identical carts approach at +2 and −2 m/s and stick together. What do you think the total momentum is after the collision?

4 · Bounciness

Now let’s add a little bounce. The same head-on pair is run at restitution e = 0.5 instead of e = 0. How much kinetic energy do you think is lost, compared with the sticking case?

5 · Watched from a moving frame

One last twist. Watch that same collision from a frame gliding along at vb = +1.5 m/s. How do you think the total momenta before and after compare in this frame?

Listen

1 · Run — stick and read the table

Press Play in Inelastic (e = 0). Watch the carts merge. Read the Momentum & energy table: Σp is equal before and after, but ΣKE is not.

2 · Predict — why do they stop?

Equal masses, +2 / −2 m/s, they stick. What happens?

3 · Restitution e

Sweep the Restitution e slider from 0 → 1. Watch ΔKE shrink as ½μ(1−e²)u²rel → 0. At e = 1 the collision is elastic.

4 · Frame beat — COM frame

Drag Frame velocity vb to equal vcm (read it in Frame invariants). In the COM frame, sticking means both carts stop. ΔKE reads the same in every frame.

5 · Explore

  • Elastic, equal masses: the velocities swap.
  • Heavy-on-light: set m₁ = 5, m₂ = 0.5, u₂ = 0 — watch v₂′ → 2u₁.
  • Explosion: the reverse of sticking — stored energy Q → KE, but Σp is still 0.

6 · Synthesise

Momentum is conserved in every collision. Kinetic energy is conserved only when elastic. ΔKE is frame-invariant. Open ∑ Formal for the algebra. Hit Finish to explore freely.

The Physics

Collisions · what this sim shows, the physics behind it, and every control

01

At a glance

Two carts collide head-on on a frictionless track, and the sim keeps a ledger of momentum and kinetic energy from before the impact to after it. You set the masses, the speeds and the bounciness, and you can watch the same crash from a moving frame.

What you'll learn

  • How to count momentum and kinetic energy for a collision, and how each total compares before and after.
  • How the restitution e sets the rebound, from sticking (e = 0) to perfectly elastic (e = 1).
  • How the kinetic energy lost depends on the masses, the approach speed and e.
  • How the same collision looks from a moving frame, and which numbers depend on the frame.
Before the impact: each cart has a mass m and a velocity v (the arrow). They meet at the dashed marker.

What's on screen

  • Cart m₁ (cyan), labelled with its mass and velocity. The arrow shows the velocity.
  • Cart m₂ (amber), labelled the same way.
  • Merged cart (violet): the two carts stuck together, or the parent body of an explosion.
  • Impact marker (dashed line): where the carts meet. The label at top left names the frame: Lab frame, or the moving frame's vb.
  • Momentum & energy: m, v, p and KE for each cart, before and after, with totals.
  • Frame invariants and Energy ledger: Σp and ΔKE, and ΣKE before and after.
See itRun m₁ = 2 kg at +3 m/s into m₂ = 1 kg at −1 m/s, with e = 0.5. Watch for: the carts meeting at the marker and leaving with new velocities, shown on screen and in the card below.

03

Momentum is conserved in every collision

Momentum has a sign, because velocity does. Kinetic energy is never negative. The sim totals both over the two carts.

The two quantities in every row of the table.

During contact the carts push on each other with equal and opposite forces for the same time. Their impulses cancel, so the total momentum cannot change, whether the carts stick, bounce or fly apart.

u is a velocity before the impact (the v₁ and v₂ sliders). v′ is a velocity after.
  • Σp can be positive, negative or zero, because the carts' momenta can cancel.
  • A stuck pair (e = 0) moves with v′ = Σp / (m₁ + m₂). If Σp = 0, the pair stops. That is momentum that was zero all along, not momentum destroyed.
See itStick m₁ = 2 kg at +3 m/s onto m₂ = 1 kg at rest. Watch for: Σp reading 6.000 kg·m/s before and after, and the stuck pair moving at +2.0 m/s.
04

Restitution sets the bounce

Two unknown final velocities need two equations. Momentum conservation gives one. The restitution e gives the other: the speed of separation is e times the speed of approach.

urel = u₁ − u₂ is the approach speed before the impact. v′rel is the relative velocity after, so it points the other way.
  • e = 0: the carts do not separate, so they stick.
  • e = 1: perfectly elastic. Separation speed equals approach speed, and kinetic energy is conserved too. Elastic mode is this case.
  • 0 < e < 1: they separate more slowly than they approached.
The same head-on start (1 kg each, ±2 m/s) at three settings of e.
See itRun two 1 kg carts at +2 and −2 m/s with e = 0.5. Watch for: the carts separating at 2.0 m/s relative to each other, half the 4.0 m/s they approached at.
See itElastic mode: m₁ = 1 kg at +2 m/s hits an identical m₂ at rest. Watch for: m₁ stopping dead and m₂ leaving at +2.0 m/s. Equal masses swap velocities.
05

How much kinetic energy is lost

Total kinetic energy splits into the motion of the centre of mass, ½Mvcm², and the motion relative to it, ½μurel², where μ = m₁m₂/(m₁ + m₂) is the reduced mass. Σp is conserved, so vcm cannot change. Only the relative part can: it starts at ½μurel² and ends at ½μe²urel².

For equal masses, μ = m/2.
m₁ m₂ u₁ (v₁) u₂ (v₂) e

These sliders move the sim too.

  • The loss grows as urel²: double the approach speed and it quadruples.
  • It scales with 1 − e², not 1 − e. At e = 0.5 the loss is still 75% of the sticking loss.
  • The sim reports how much kinetic energy is lost, not where it goes (heat, sound, permanent deformation).
See itRun the same head-on pair (1 kg each, ±2 m/s) at e = 0, 0.5 and 1. Watch for: three runs in turn, and the card listing ΔKE for each: −4, −3 and 0 J.
06

What a moving frame changes

Watched from a frame moving at vb, every velocity becomes v′ = v − vb. That is what the Frame velocity slider does.

Here Σp′ and ΔKE′ are measured in the moving frame; vb is its velocity in the lab.
  • Σp shifts by (m₁ + m₂)vb, by the same amount before and after. So it is still conserved in every frame.
  • ΔKE does not change, because it depends only on urel and a boost leaves urel alone.
  • At vb = vcm = Σp / (m₁ + m₂), the total momentum is zero. A stuck pair then stops.
See itStick two 1 kg carts at +2 and −2 m/s, watched from vb = +1.5 m/s. Watch for: Σp reading −3.000 kg·m/s before and after, while ΔKE still reads −4.000 J.
See itStick m₁ = 2 kg at +3 m/s onto m₂ = 1 kg at rest, with two cameras. Watch for: the lab view above carrying the stuck pair on at +2.0 m/s, and the view below, moving at vcm = +2.0 m/s, showing it at rest.
07

An explosion is a collision run backwards

One body of mass M = m₁ + m₂ starts at rest and splits in two. Stored energy Q turns into kinetic energy, and Σp stays 0, so the fragments move off with equal and opposite momenta p*.

μ = m₁m₂/(m₁ + m₂), the same reduced mass as in a collision.
  • Since KE = p²/2m, the lighter fragment carries the larger share of Q: KEA / KEB = mB / mA.
  • The sim treats Q as released from a store (a spring, a chemical charge). It does not model what the store is.
See itExplode a body into m₁ = 1 kg and m₂ = 3 kg with Q = 4 J. Watch for: the 1 kg fragment leaving at +2.4 m/s and the 3 kg fragment at −0.8 m/s, with Σp still 0.
08

Where it matters

  • Ballistic pendulum. A bullet embeds in a hanging block. Momentum conservation gives the speed just after the impact, and energy conservation after it gives the swing height. A 10 g bullet at 100 m/s into a 1.0 kg block leaves the pair at 0.99 m/s, rising 5.0 cm. Only about 1% of the bullet's kinetic energy is left to swing.
  • Crumple zones. A car body is built to deform. The kinetic energy goes into bending metal, and the longer stopping time lowers the average force on the passengers (F = Δp/Δt).
  • Neutron moderation. In a reactor, neutrons slow down by hitting light nuclei. Treat the collision as elastic and head-on, with the nucleus at rest: the neutron can hand over at most 4m₁m₂/(m₁ + m₂)² of its energy. That is nearly all of it for a proton (almost the same mass as a neutron), and under 30% for carbon-12.
Go deeper: the elastic closed forms
The e = 1 solution, which Elastic mode uses.
  • Equal masses swap velocities: v₁′ = u₂ and v₂′ = u₁.
  • A heavy cart hitting a light one at rest gives it nearly 2u₁. With m₁ = 5 kg, m₂ = 0.5 kg and u₁ = 3 m/s the sim shows v₂′ = 5.45 m/s.
  • A light cart hitting a heavy one at rest bounces back with nearly −u₁.
09

Summary

In one line. Σp is the same before and after every collision, whatever e is. Kinetic energy is lost by an amount ½μ(1 − e²)urel², which every frame agrees on.

Key points

  • Equal and opposite contact forces keep Σp fixed. e then fixes the separation speed.
  • e = 0 sticks, e = 1 is elastic. Only elastic collisions conserve kinetic energy.
  • The kinetic energy lost depends on μ, urel and e, and not on the frame.
  • Σp depends on the frame. It is zero in the centre-of-mass frame.

Common mix-ups

  • "If kinetic energy vanishes when carts stick, momentum must vanish too." Internal forces cancel in Σp, and kinetic energy has somewhere to go (heat, deformation).
  • "At e = 0.5 half of the sticking loss is left." The loss scales with 1 − e², so 75% of it is lost.
  • "Momentum is conserved only in the lab frame." It is conserved in every Galilean frame. Its value changes with the frame, and its constancy does not.

Things to try on your own

  • Choose masses and speeds that give Σp = 0, set e = 0, and read the Momentum & energy table after the impact.
  • Set m₁ = 5 kg, m₂ = 0.5 kg, v₂ = 0 in Elastic mode, and compare v₂′ with 2v₁.
  • With e = 0 and unequal masses, drag the Frame velocity slider until Σp after reads 0, and compare vb with vcm.
